content:
anika_pm: Hey all 4B0 noticed my May net pay dropped by ~€1,200 vs usual. Gross looks like my normal salary but theres a line for US federal withholding. Im on Dutch payroll (NL) and we converted my contractor record to employee last month. Anyone see why?

paul_payroll: Thanks for flagging. Can you paste the stub lines (redacted) and confirm your payroll country code in Workday? Conversions can sometimes double-up records during the first synced run.

anika_pm: Redacted stub: 

```
Pay date: 05/28/2026
Gross EUR: 8,400.00
Nederland belasting: 1,680.00
Sociale verzekering: 620.00
US federal tax: 1,200.00
Net EUR: 4,900.00
```

rita_hr: I see the conversion in HR was completed on 05/15/2026 but the vendor/contractor profile (which was US-tax-tagged) wasn't fully archived before the May payroll snapshot. That likely caused a duplicate US-file entry. I'll mark the vendor record inactive and add a note.

sam_finance: Operational note: if the US withholding remitted, reversal depends on whether the payment cleared our US processor. If it cleared we'll need to either reclaim or issue an employer-side correction and potentially a W-2/W-2c if a US wage record was created. Paul, can you check remittance status?

payroll-bot: Payroll run 2026-05-28 processed. Batch id pr-20260528-7721. Files sent to NL and US channels.

paul_payroll: Confirmed: US channel received a record for employee id 11567 on 05/28 and remittance file submitted 05/29 13:42 UTC. Bank settlement shows ACH initiation 05/30 so funds likely in transit. We'll try to halt the ACH but if it settles we'll proceed with reclaim. Ticket PAY-INTL-9445 opened.

anika_pm: If reclaim succeeds, will I get a single correction line or a full off-cycle payment? Im counting on that difference for rent.

paul_payroll: If we can stop/recall before settlement finalizes, we will simply post an adjustment reversing the US withholding and youll see a correction line on your next stub. If funds settle and we can reclaim from processor, well post an off-cycle credit. If reclaim fails, Finance may issue an interim reimbursement to cover your net shortfall while we pursue recovery. We try to avoid asking employees to file refund claims personally.

rita_hr: Also note: because you converted from contractor to employee, we need a signed employment start date form to set the correct tax effective date. Ill DM you the form to confirm the conversion effective 05/01/2026 so payroll knows to attribute May wages to NL.

anika_pm: I signed and uploaded it just now. Thanks.

sam_finance: Two actions from Finance: (1) If reclaim fails, we will gross-up the interim reimbursement to cover tax differences so you arent penalized, (2) we'll ensure year-end reporting is correct (no US 1099/W-2 for NL employees). We'll also log this as a process gap on conversions.

paul_payroll: Updating ticket PAY-INTL-9445: attempting ACH stop with payment ops, ETA 48 hours. If stop fails, off-cycle reversal target 7 business days post-reclaim. Ill post interim stub examples so you know what to expect.

anika_pm: Appreciate the help. One more Q 914 should I expect any tax forms to file in the US because of this transient record? Im not a US citizen and never worked there.

sam_finance: Unlikely if we successfully reverse before W-2/1099 issuance. If a US file was processed and not fully reversed, we may need to issue corrected forms (W-2c/1099-c) and help you with the refund paper trail. We'll coordinate with our tax counsel and keep employee action minimal.

rita_hr: Ill follow up in 24 hours after the vendor deactivation and attach the signed employment confirmation to the ticket. Thanks for reporting this quickly.

payroll-bot: PAY-INTL-9445 created and assigned to paul_payroll. Estimated resolution: 2026-06-11.
